title: Derivative of a product Gaussian density
statement: Let $I$ be a finite index set, let $v\ge0$, and let $c,z\in\mathbb R^I$. The function $m\mapsto\prod_{i\in I}p_v(m_i,z_i)$ is differentiable at $c$, with derivative the linear functional $h\mapsto\sum_{i\in I}\bigl(\prod_{j\ne i}p_v(c_j,z_j)\bigr)((z_i-c_i)/v)p_v(c_i,z_i)h_i$, where $p_v$ is the Gaussian density of variance $v$ and division by zero is interpreted as zero.
replaced: Let $I$ be finite and $v\ge0$. Write $p_v(c,z)$ for the $N(c,v)$ density when $v>0$ and set $p_0(c,z)=0$; define $G_v(c,z)=\prod_{i\in I}p_v(c_i,z_i)$ and interpret division by zero as zero. Let $A_v(c,z)$ be the linear functional $h\mapsto\sum_i\bigl(\prod_{j\ne i}p_v(c_j,z_j)\bigr)((z_i-c_i)/v)p_v(c_i,z_i)h_i$. For every $c,z\in\mathbb R^I$, the derivative at $c$ of $m\mapsto G_v(m,z)$ is $A_v(c,z)$.
